newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cinema bomb kills two, wounds 20 in Algerian capital.
newsitem.headline: Cinema bomb kills two, wounds 20 in Algerian capital.

text.p: Fresh violence returned to Algeria's capital on Thursday when a bomb ripped through a crowded central cinema, killing two people and wounding around 20.
The bomb was the first to hit Algiers since the country held general elections on June 5 which President Liamine Zeroual hopes will help end years of violence.

It followed newspaper reports earlier on Thursday of new massacres in isolated villages in which 26 people, including six children and a pregnant woman, were killed by suspected Moslem fundamentalists.
"The bomb was put under a seat," a witness told Reuters by telephone. "It wasn't a very powerful bomb but the cinema was crowded."
Thursday is a holiday in Moslem Algeria. Ambulances rushed to the cinema, the "Sindbad", in the city centre, eyewitnesses said.
Security forces said the bomb went off at 2.55 p.m. (1355 GMT) and that the toll was provisional.
In a statement carried by the official news agency APS, they said the bomb "according to an initial toll had killed two people and wounded around 20 in the Sindbad cinema in Omar Bencheikh Street.
"Rescue services and security forces went immediately to the spot to help the victims," it said.
The blast was the first in the city of between three and four million people since a bomb killed seven people and wounded 37 on June 2, the final day of campaigning for the election.
The ballot was the first multi-party parliamentary election since the authorities in January 1992 scrapped one in which Moslem fundamentalist had taken a huge lead.
About 60,000 people have died in the violence since.

Thursday's explosion and reports in the main Arabic language paper Al Khabar of the killings underscored the pitiless conflict still shaking the North African country despite its focus on political events following the June election.
Al Khabar said 11 died in one attack and 15 in the second.
Another newspaper, the independent El Watan, also reported the massacre of the 15 who died, in Jaouaza village, near Lardjem, Tissemsilt province.
There was no official confirmation of the killings.

But diplomats say the fact two of the main newspapers reported them is effective confirmation, in the light of the authorities' huge powers to act against newspapers which carry security reports which the authorities may challenge.
Al Khabar said a group of "terrorists" -- Algerian shorthand for Moslem fundamentalists -- attacked the isolated Jaouaza village in the Ouarsenis mountain range early on Tuesday.

They arrived at 4 a.m. and tried to force the women to leave the village with them. When they refused, 15 of the inhabitants were killed. Among them were six children and three women, one of whom was pregnant.
Al Khabar said that earlier this week, another group killed 11 people in a village 50 km (30 miles) from Bechar, a provincial capital about 775 km (480 miles) southwest of Algiers.
Since last Saturday, Algerian newspapers have reported at least three other massacres, including one of five members of the same family who had their throats cut in a house in Algiers.
Al Khabar on Thursday said security forces had wiped out 10 "terrorists" in a search operation over four days this week in the western Tlemcen area.
